=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1480-1497 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The bash rewrite dropped the original Python word-boundary anchors, so repo-scoped issue references can match inside longer strings or suffix-bearing issue-like text.
  WHY: The original regex used `\b` boundaries to block false positives like `someotherowner/repo/issues/5678`, `Fixes #12a`, and `owner/repo/issues/123-draft`, so removing them changes the parser to accept substrings.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1489-1497 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `_repository_escaped` only escapes dots, so repository names containing other regex metacharacters can break matching or change regex meaning.
  WHY: Leaving characters like `+`, `*`, `?`, `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`, `^`, `$`, `|`, and `\` unescaped makes the grep patterns unsafe for valid repository strings.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1483-1489 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: Dropping the owner/repo shape validation means malformed repository strings are silently accepted and fed into the regex matcher.
  WHY: Inputs like `repo` or `owner/repo/extra` no longer fail the prior guard, so the helper can return spurious matches or an empty result instead of surfacing the bad caller input.
- scripts/review_collect_pr_metadata.sh:112-121 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: When the optional reviews fetch fails, `PR_REVIEWS_FILE` remains `[]`, so failure is indistinguishable from a real zero-review result.
  WHY: Downstream consumers lose the ability to tell a break-glass/API failure from an intentionally empty review set, which hides permission and rate-limit problems.
- scripts/review_collect_pr_metadata.sh:111-121 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Non-truthy or unrecognized `REVIEW_BREAK_GLASS_ENABLED` values silently skip the optional reviews fetch with no diagnostic.
  WHY: Misconfigured feature-flag values therefore behave like disabled mode without warning, making the break-glass path hard to debug.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:820-841 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The cached post-merge JSON validation still falls back to live GraphQL when the cache is malformed, so the cache is not the single source of truth on that path.
  WHY: A malformed cache can reintroduce extra API calls and bad issue data into the merge-dispatch flow instead of failing on the cached inputs alone.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1489-1497 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The grep rewrite of `extract_repo_scoped_issue_refs_from_text` dropped the word-boundary anchors (`\b`) that the original Python version carried on every pattern.
  WHY: A substring like `someowner/repo/issues/12` will incorrectly match `owner/repo/issues/12` because there's no `\b` before `owner`, causing spurious issue extraction.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1493 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The shell rewrite only escapes dots in `_repository_escaped` (`${_repository//./\\.}`), but other regex metacharacters are not escaped.
  WHY: Repository names with characters like `+`, `*`, `?`, `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`, `^`, `$`, and `|` can fail to match valid issue references or match incorrectly.
- scripts/review_collect_pr_metadata.sh:112-121 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the optional reviews fetch fails under `REVIEW_BREAK_GLASS_ENABLED=true`, the script writes a warning but leaves `PR_REVIEWS_FILE` as the empty `[]` written before the fetch attempt.
  WHY: Downstream consumers cannot distinguish a failed optional fetch from an intentionally empty review set, making debugging misconfigurations difficult.
- scripts/review_collect_pr_metadata.sh:112 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The case statement only matches `1|true|yes|on` and silently skips fetching for any other value, including invalid inputs like `enabled`, `yesplease`, or `on_`.
  WHY: A misconfiguration like `REVIEW_BREAK_GLASS_ENABLED=enabled` will silently not fetch reviews with no warning, making debugging difficult.

  Expected change site: .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml, ready-to-merge / review-blocked label-reconciliation paths
  Evidence of absence: The PR only updated the gate job + post-merge-validate-dispatch path. The ready-to-merge and review-blocked label-setting steps still read from `PR_META_FILE` but were not updated to consume the new gate-output caches (`post_merge_pr_text_json`, `post_merge_linked_issues_json`) as a fallback before the live `/pulls` call.
